finding.summary: Canonical browser PTY input reaches an attached normal tmux client. Current main had per-user tmux sockets but no immutable managed tmux configuration, so default tmux control bindings remained a potential alternate command/process surface outside Claude Code and EffectGate.
primary_upstream_basis: tmux Getting Started: default prefix is C-b and C-b c runs new-window; tmux key bindings execute tmux commands; user .tmux.conf is read when the server starts

OpenBSD tmux(1): default-command empty creates a login shell using default-shell; new-session/new-window accept multiple command arguments and execute them directly without sh -c; global -f selects a configuration file
finding.strongest_counterhypothesis: The browser/xterm path might suppress the relevant control-byte sequence in the exact packaged runtime. Current ClayVerse source does not itself establish such suppression: browser terminal input is encoded and binary PTY frames are only size-bounded before being written to the PTY. Exact packaged runtime fault injection is still required.

repair.donor: closed PR #427 contained the unmerged managed-tmux policy concept; canonical main had fused only its per-user socket portion
changes: add root-owned /etc/clayverse/tmux.conf and pass it through tmux -f on has-session/new-session/attach paths
disable prefix/prefix2 and unbind prefix/root key tables; disable status and mouse
set default-shell to the existing fail-closed deny-shell guard
pass the initial env/Claude command as direct tmux argv instead of one shell-command string so startup does not require sh -c
